issues.description: The type of the Person.id field is inconsistent across the artifacts. The problem statement's UML and the template repository define Person.id as java.util.UUID, and the server/service code in the template expects UUID (e.g. uses UUID.randomUUID(), endpoint path variables typed as UUID). In the solution repository, the common Person model defines id as Long while the solution's server/service code still treats IDs as UUID. This mismatch (UUID vs Long) will confuse students and makes the solution repository internally inconsistent and uncompilable (e.g. calling setId(UUID) where setId expects Long, comparing Long to UUID).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Person.id type consistent across all artifacts. The simplest fix preserving the problem statement intent is to change the solution repository's common Person model to use java.util.UUID for id (update the field, getter, setter, and import). Ensure the common Person.id type matches the server/service and resource method signatures that use UUID (e.g. UUID.randomUUID(), @PathVariable UUID). Alternatively, if Long is desired, update the problem statement, template service/resource code, and all usages to consistently use Long, but changing the solution's Person model back to UUID is recommended to align with the exercise description.

issues.description: Within the solution repository there is an internal type mismatch: server/service code expects and manipulates UUID IDs (e.g. PersonService.setId(UUID.randomUUID()), PersonResource path variables are UUID), while the solution's shared Person model defines id as Long. This inner-solution inconsistency will cause compile-time errors and prevents the solution from being a valid reference implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Fix the solution repository so its model and server code agree on the ID type. Update solution_repository/src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java to use UUID for id (with appropriate import), or change all usages in PersonService and PersonResource to Long. Given the problem statement and template use UUID, the recommended correction is to change the common Person.id back to UUID and ensure getters/setters and all uses match UUID.

issues.description: The Person.id concept is represented inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement and the template use UUID for Person IDs, while the solution's Common Person model declares id as Long. Server-side code in the solution (PersonResource, PersonService) still uses UUID in method signatures/parameters, which mismatches the solution Person model. This inconsistency breaks the conceptual mapping of “Person identifier” (students expect a UUID ID per the exercise) and will cause confusion and likely compile/runtime problems when comparing or validating IDs across request path variables and Person objects.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Person identifier type consistent across all artifacts. Prefer aligning to the exercise description and template (use java.util.UUID for Person.id). Concretely, change the solution's common Person.id type from Long to UUID (update getter/setter types), and ensure PersonService and PersonResource use UUID everywhere for parameters and comparisons. Alternatively, if Long is desired, update the problem statement and template to specify Long IDs and adapt all server/client/service signatures accordingly — but do not mix types.
